instructions: Read the complete rendering policy through read_policy. For each independent artifact case, transform the supplied draft or source into the requested output and persist it through write_output. These are isolated human-facing outputs; preserve their facts and use the supplied source material. Do not query a tracker or read additional files. Separately answer every bounded rule question. Global operator guidance applies. Finish after every case is recorded.

tools.name: read_policy
tools.description: Read the unchanged policy in bounded chunks. Start at offset 0, then use each returned next_offset until it is null. Complete policy delivery is required before workflow operations. No scratch file is needed.

tools.name: write_output
tools.description: Persist the completed rendering for one artifact case. Write once per case; provide the actual normalised text or violation report requested.

tools.name: answer_rule
tools.description: Answer one separate bounded policy question in its stated value shape. Do not perform hypothetical actions.

tools.name: finish
tools.description: Finish after all artifacts and rule answers are recorded.

decision.title: Persist recovery tokens in SQLite
decision.chosen: Use the existing SQLite database for recovery tokens.

source.spec_rationale: One local service must retain token state across restart; the existing database avoids a second persistence service.
source.implementation_evidence: The committed implementation writes a token row before acknowledging creation. A restart test passes. No multi-host deployment or throughput test was performed.

decision.title: Deduplicate webhook jobs
decision.chosen: Use a unique delivery key in the existing job table.

source.spec_rationale: The provider may deliver the same event twice. The service already has a job table with a unique-key constraint.
source.implementation_evidence: The same delivery key is inserted once and the second enqueue is acknowledged without a second job. A duplicate-event test passes. Different event ordering was not changed.

decision.title: Use a durable retry ledger
decision.chosen: Keep retry attempts in the existing durable database.

source.spec_rationale: The accepted transient retry record in ADR-0041 loses attempt history after restart. This settled choice preserves that history.
source.implementation_evidence: The retry count and next-attempt time survive the tested restart. No ADR status or supersession metadata has been changed; the caller owns recording it.
